title: Quasi-coherent direct sums and sections on a quasi-compact algebraic stack
statement:
Use the universes and small indexing sets of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Quasi-coherent modules are module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on its big fppf site, locally admitting presentations by small sums of the structure sheaf, as in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. For every small set $A$ and family $(F_a)_{a\in A}$ of quasi-coherent modules, their coproduct $F=\bigoplus_{a\in A}F_a$, characterized by $\operatorname{Hom}(F,G)=\prod_{a\in A}\operatorname{Hom}(F_a,G)$, exists in quasi-coherent modules and agrees with the coproduct in all module sheaves (the sheafification of the presheaf direct sum). For every scheme test $x:T\to\mathcal X$, let $F_x$ and $(F_a)_x$ be the quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_T$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] attached to $x$ by the scheme-test restriction of [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction], with tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]; the summand maps induce a canonical isomorphism $\bigoplus_{a\in A}(F_a)_x\xrightarrow{\sim}F_x$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_T$-modules. If $\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact, meaning that it admits a smooth surjective atlas from a quasi-compact scheme [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], the canonical map
$$\bigoplus_{a\in A}\Gamma(\mathcal X,F_a)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma\left(\mathcal X,\bigoplus_{a\in A}F_a\right)$$
is an isomorphism of $\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})$-modules, natural in the family. Global sections have the compatible-family meaning of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. No quasi-separatedness, separation of the diagonal, finiteness of $A$, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06WN (lemma-qc-colimits), part (1) and its proof by scheme-test restriction; stacks-properties.tex Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), parts (2),(3). The global-section assertion is the finite-support descent consequence for a quasi-compact smooth atlas; it needs no quasi-separatedness.

proof.text: Form the presheaf of modules $P(x)=\bigoplus_{a\in A}F_a(x)$ with componentwise restrictions. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], its module sheafification $F=P^\#$, with the canonical summand maps $\iota_a:F_a\to F$, is the coproduct in all module sheaves. The size convention makes the discrete diagram on $A$ small, so that the cited existence statement applies. This construction also applies when $A$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), coproduct construction in its proof

proof.text: Fix any scheme test $x:T\to\mathcal X$. By [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction], write the restriction of $F_a$ to the big fppf slice over $x$ as $A_T((F_a)_x)$, where $A_T(M)(u:T\prime\to T)=\Gamma(T\prime,u^*M)$. The ambient Zariski coproduct $N_x=\bigoplus_a(F_a)_x$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-coproduct-closure]. The functor $A_T$ preserves small colimits by [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence], and restriction to this slice preserves them by [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-ringed-inverse-image]. Consequently $F|_x\simeq\bigoplus_a A_T((F_a)_x)\simeq A_T(N_x)$, with each summand map the stated canonical one. In particular $F|_x$ is quasi-coherent. Its local free presentations are presentations of $F$ on the same localized site objects; doing this for every $x$ supplies local presentations at every object of the big site. Thus $F$ is quasi-coherent by the local-presentation definition in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Apply scheme-test restriction now to $F$. Full faithfulness of $A_T$ identifies $N_x\xrightarrow{\sim}F_x$, since their images and summand maps are the preceding coproduct. Uniqueness of this identification makes it natural in the family and compatible with scheme-test pullback. Finally the quasi-coherent category is full in module sheaves, so the ambient coproduct universal property restricts to the asserted Hom bijection for every quasi-coherent $G$.

source.place: Tag 06WN (lemma-qc-colimits)(1), proof via scheme slices; Tag 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent); descent.tex Tags 03DX and 06VE

proof.text: For each $b\in A$, the coproduct universal property defines $\pi_b:F\to F_b$ by $\pi_b\iota_a=1$ if $a=b$ and $0$ otherwise. A global section $s$ of a module $H$ is equivalently a module map $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\to H$: its component sends $r$ to $r s_x$, and evaluation at $1$ gives the inverse, by the compatible-family definition in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. The structure module is quasi-coherent, with its rank-one free presentation. In particular every $s\in\Gamma(\mathcal X,F)$ has global coordinates $s_b=\pi_b(s)$. Applying $\pi_b$ to a finite sum $\sum_a\iota_a(t_a)$ recovers $t_b$. The canonical map from the direct sum of the global sections is therefore injective, without any compactness assumption.

source.place: Tag 06TV (definition-structure-sheaf); compatible-family global sections and the coproduct universal property

proof.text: Assume now that $\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact. Choose a smooth surjective atlas $u:U\to\mathcal X$ with $U$ quasi-compact, as allowed by [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] and the finite-subcover definition [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], choose a finite affine open cover $(V_j)$ of $U$. Fix $s\in\Gamma(\mathcal X,F)$. For each test $x_j:V_j\to\mathcal X$, step 2 identifies $F_{x_j}$ with the ambient coproduct of $(F_a)_{x_j}$. Its apex and summands are quasi-coherent, so [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-evaluation] with the small discrete category $A$ identifies its sections on the affine open $V_j$ itself with $\bigoplus_a\Gamma(V_j,(F_a)_{x_j})$. Hence $s|_{V_j}$ has finite support $J_j\subseteq A$. Put $J=\bigcup_j J_j$, a finite set. The coordinate identities from step 3 give $s|_{V_j}=\sum_{a\in J}\iota_a(s_a)|_{V_j}$ for every $j$. The Zariski sheaf condition on $U$ gives $s|_U=\sum_{a\in J}\iota_a(s_a)|_U$. If $U$ is empty the cover and $J$ may both be empty, and the same equality holds.

Let $t=s-\sum_{a\in J}\iota_a(s_a)$. By step 4 its section on $U$ is zero. Under the section/map identification of step 3 it gives a quasi-coherent module map $m_t:\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\to F$. Its restriction to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ is zero: on each etale scheme $W\to U$ the restricted map is multiplication by the pullback of $t|_U=0$, by the natural scheme-test section comparison [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction]. The equivalence [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-module-descent] is given on morphisms by this restriction, hence is faithful. It follows that $m_t=0$, and thus $t=0$. Therefore $s=\sum_{a\in J}\iota_a(s_a)$ is in the image of the canonical section map. This proves surjectivity. This use of the atlas equivalence requires only its faithfulness; its statement allows arbitrary algebraic-space relation spaces, with no quasi-separatedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), faithfulness of restriction for a smooth presentation; scheme-test formula of Tags 06WI and 06WK

proof.text: The section map is $\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})$-linear: each $\iota_a$ is a module map, so $\iota_a(r t)=r\iota_a(t)$ objectwise, and finite summation preserves this equality. It is natural because a family of module maps $v_a:F_a\to G_a$ induces the unique coproduct map $v$ with $v\iota_a=\iota_a v_a$; evaluating this equality on global sections gives the naturality square. Injectivity from step 3 and surjectivity from step 5 therefore give the asserted natural module isomorphism. Empty families and zero modules obey the same formulas. Only the finite affine cover of $U$ used compactness; no property of the overlaps or diagonal, or finiteness of $A$, was used.

lean.statement: theorem moduli_qcoh_direct_sums {S : Scheme.{u}} (C : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hC : IsAlgebraicModuliStack C) (A : Type (max (u + 1) v w)) (F : A → ModuliQCoh C hC.1.1) : ∃ c : Cofan F, Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit ((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (moduliModuleRings C hC.1.1)).ι.mapCocone c)) ∧ (∀ (r : ModuliSchemeRestriction C hC.1.1) (x : C.obj), Nonempty (IsColimit ((r.restriction x).mapCocone c))) ∧ (IsQuasiCompactModuli C → Nonempty (IsColimit (((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (moduliModuleRings C hC.1.1)).ι ⋙ moduliModuleGlobalSections C hC.1.1).mapCocone c)))
lean.note: Uses the existing ModuliQCoh full subcategory and ModuliSchemeRestriction. Colimiting cofans retain the actual summand maps: the same cofan is colimiting in ambient module sheaves, on every scheme test, and after global sections when the stack is quasi-compact. The global section functor is the compatible-family submodule with the pointwise action of the recorded global regular-function ring. These structural helpers have real data; the single theorem proof is postponed.
